name: Norepinephrine (noradrenaline)
executiveSummary: First-line vasopressor in septic shock. Adult: start **0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min** (or **4–8 mcg/min**) titrate to MAP. Pediatrics/NICU: **0.05–1 mcg/kg/min** (usual max **2 mcg/kg/min**). Central line + pump.
indications:
## Indications

- Vasodilated shock (septic) with hypotension despite volume.
- Other shocks with low SVR.

## Precautions

- Digital/mesenteric ischemia; arrhythmias; extravasation → necrosis (treat with local phentolamine per protocol).
- Prefer D5W as diluent in many institutional guides (oxidation in NS).

> Does not replace fluid resuscitation or treatment of the cause.

adulto.diluent: Prefer D5W; NS per local monograph.
adulto.dose: Start **0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min** or **4–8 mcg/min**; titrate (common ranges **8–12 mcg/min**; high **>30 mcg/min** ICU only).
adulto.notes: Monitor MAP, lactate, urine output, peripheral perfusion.

pediatrico.notes: Do not use if brown discoloration. Discard remainder.

neonatal.dose: **0.05–1 mcg/kg/min** continuous IV; titrate to MAP/perfusion (common max **1–2 mcg/kg/min**).

stability:
## Stability

- Protect from light. Pump dilution: ~24 h at room temperature (local guide). Discard if oxidized.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypertension, reflex bradycardia, ischemia, necrosis from extravasation, arrhythmias.
